motivation: Accurate numerical approximation of the ground state energy of Bose-Einstein condensates is important for understanding quantum many-body systems, but standard conforming finite elements may not provide guaranteed lower bounds.
method: The authors use nonconforming finite element spaces (specifically the Crouzeix-Raviart element) to discretize the Gross-Pitaevskii energy functional and derive a priori error estimates for the discrete ground state energy, eigenvalue, and state.
result: Explicit convergence rates are obtained for the Crouzeix-Raviart element, and it is proven that the discrete ground state energy provides a lower bound to the exact energy. Numerical experiments confirm the theoretical results.
conclusion: The nonconforming finite element approach offers a reliable way to compute lower bounds for the Gross-Pitaevskii ground state energy, which can be useful for benchmarking and validation in BEC simulations.

title: Observing Joinings: A Distance-Array Characterization Of Furstenberg Disjointness
authors: Ao Xu
abstract: ArXiv:2605.23349v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Joinings are fundamental global objects in ergodic theory, yet in compact metric models one naturally observes only finite orbit-distance patterns. We bridge this gap by introducing multi-particle distance arrays, which sample finite orbit segments and record their joint metric evolution. In the anchored fixed-model setting, this framework yields a purely finite-observable characterization of Furstenberg disjointness: two systems are disjoint if and only if all their anchored multi-orbit distance-array projections are independent. The structural engine behind this criterion is a marked and colored version of the Gromov--Vershik reconstruction principle for exchangeable arrays; unanchored arrays reconstruct the intrinsic twin-free quotient, while anchors recover the actual joining in a fixed model. To quantify this independence, we introduce Wasserstein dependence coefficients, establishing an all-order zero criterion for disjointness, and show that weak neighborhoods of the product joining always admit finite distance-array certificates. Examples from compact rotations, Bernoulli and reversible Markov shifts, common factors, Kronecker factors, and weak mixing demonstrate the strict necessity of the multi-particle level and the broad scope of this approach.
tldr: This paper introduces a finite-observable characterization of Furstenberg disjointness in ergodic theory using multi-particle distance arrays.
motivation: To bridge the gap between global joinings in ergodic theory and finite orbit-distance patterns observable in compact metric models.
method: Develops multi-particle distance arrays and a marked/colored version of the Gromov–Vershik reconstruction principle for exchangeable arrays.
result: Establishes that two systems are disjoint iff all anchored multi-orbit distance-array projections are independent, and introduces Wasserstein dependence coefficients for quantification.
conclusion: Provides a purely finite-observable criterion for disjointness with examples from rotations, Bernoulli shifts, and weak mixing, but the work is purely mathematical and not directly applicable to the user's research interests.

title: Layered Construction Of Message-Wise Unequal Error Protection Codes
authors: Qiming Lu, Shan Lu, Takaya Yamazato
abstract: ArXiv:2605.23390v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Conventional communication systems are mainly designed to reduce error rates and increase transmission rates, and therefore usually provide uniform protection to all transmitted messages. However, in intent-oriented applications, different messages may have different semantic meanings and importance levels, requiring different levels of reliability. This paper proposes a layered construction of message-level unequal error protection (UEP) codes for short-blocklength communication. Instead of appending an explicit protection tag to each codeword, the proposed method embeds the protection structure directly into the Hamming-distance structure of the codebook. By assigning larger minimum intra-level distances to higher-importance message groups and imposing suitable inter-level distance constraints, the proposed codebook provides differentiated error-correction capabilities while enabling reliable importance-level classification at the receiver. Theoretical conditions for correct group classification are derived, and simulations over AWGN and VLC-ISI channels show that the proposed scheme improves BER performance and group classification accuracy compared with a tag-based ECC baseline.
tldr: This paper proposes a layered construction of message-wise unequal error protection codes for short-blocklength communication, embedding protection structure into the Hamming-distance structure of the codebook.
motivation: Conventional communication systems provide uniform protection, but intent-oriented applications require different reliability levels for messages of varying importance.
method: The method assigns larger minimum intra-level distances to higher-importance message groups and imposes inter-level distance constraints, enabling differentiated error correction and reliable importance-level classification at the receiver.
result: Simulations over AWGN and VLC-ISI channels show improved BER performance and group classification accuracy compared to a tag-based ECC baseline.
conclusion: The proposed scheme offers a promising approach for short-blocklength UEP without explicit tags, with potential applications in semantic and intent-oriented communication.

title: Stochastic Generalized Sampling
authors: Matteo Santacesaria Luca Finotti
abstract: ArXiv:2605.23421v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Reconstructing an infinite-dimensional signal from a finite set of measurements is a fundamental problem in approximation theory and signal processing. While the generalized sampling (GS) framework provides a robust methodology for recovering elements in arbitrary separable Hilbert spaces, deterministic approaches suffer from severe basis-dependent dimensionality constraints, often requiring a quadratic sample complexity [MATH] to avoid numerical instability. In this paper, we introduce a fully stochastic framework for GS that natively overcomes these deterministic barriers. By drawing measurements according to an optimal leverage-score probability distribution, we prove that stable recovery is guaranteed with high probability at a near-linear sample complexity of [MATH]. Crucially, this optimal rate is universal-independent of the specific choice of measurement and reconstruction bases-and holds even when the sensing system is a highly redundant frame. To establish these guarantees, we derive a novel matrix Bernstein inequality for random rectangular operators, allowing us to rigorously control the aliasing error governed by the empirical cross-term. Finally, we demonstrate the practical efficacy of our approach on the classical problem of recovering analytic functions from continuous Fourier measurements via Legendre polynomials, where our randomized method achieve near-exponential convergence rates.
tldr: This paper introduces a stochastic framework for generalized sampling that achieves near-linear sample complexity, overcoming deterministic quadratic barriers.
motivation: Deterministic generalized sampling suffers from quadratic sample complexity due to basis-dependent constraints, limiting its applicability.
method: The authors propose drawing measurements according to an optimal leverage-score probability distribution and derive a novel matrix Bernstein inequality for random rectangular operators.
result: Stable recovery is guaranteed with high probability at near-linear sample complexity, independent of the choice of bases.
conclusion: The randomized method achieves near-exponential convergence for recovering analytic functions from Fourier measurements, with potential for broader signal processing applications.

title: Sparse In-Network Learning Via Shortest-Path Backpropagation And Finite-Rate Gating
authors: Mohammad Reza Deylam Salehi
abstract: ArXiv:2605.23424v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In-network learning (INL) trains distributed neural modules by exchanging latent activations and backpropagated errors over a communication graph. This letter proposes Dijkstra-pruned INL (D-INL), which removes non-tree links by retaining a capacity-aware shortest-path tree rooted at the fusion node. To balance sparsity and predictive information, local routing (or aggregation) is modeled as a finite-rate stochastic gate with rate [MATH]. We derive a rate-distortion-generalization bound and validate the method on a reproducible distributed-classification experiment, where D-INL reduces training exchange by [MATH] while preserving accuracy within the standard deviation of dense INL. Adding finite-rate regularization further reduces the estimated latent rate by [MATH] relative to unregularized Dijkstra INL.
tldr: This paper proposes a sparse in-network learning method using shortest-path backpropagation and finite-rate gating to reduce communication overhead in distributed neural network training.
motivation: To reduce the communication cost of in-network learning while maintaining accuracy, as dense communication graphs are inefficient.
method: Dijkstra-pruned INL (D-INL) removes non-tree links by retaining a capacity-aware shortest-path tree, and models local routing as a finite-rate stochastic gate with rate-distortion regularization.
result: D-INL reduces training exchange by a factor while preserving accuracy within the standard deviation of dense INL; finite-rate regularization further reduces latent rate.
conclusion: The method demonstrates that sparse communication graphs can achieve comparable accuracy to dense ones, with potential applications in distributed machine learning systems.

title: Rate-induced Tipping In A Coral Reef Ecosystem: A Slow Increase In Fishing Effort Can Induce Reef Collapse
authors: Irakli Antidze, Brian Hennessy, Nikola Popovic, Zak Sattar
abstract: ArXiv:2605.23487v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Critical transitions describe sudden changes in the state of an ecosystem. In classical bifurcation theory, such transitions occur when the value of a parameter exceeds a threshold (``bifurcation") value. More recently, critical transitions which are triggered by the rate of change of a parameter were described by Wieczorek et al. [Wieczorek, S., Ashwin, P., Luke, C.M., Cox, P.M., Proceedings of the Royal Society A 467(2129), 1243-1269, 2011]. In mathematical ecology, these rate-induced transitions correspond to environmental conditions that deteriorate too rapidly for the ecosystem to adapt, resulting in population collapse (``R-tipping"). In this article, we consider the potential for rate-induced tipping due to increased anthropogenic stress in a recently proposed behavioural-demographic model for herbivorous fish, algae, and coral in a coral reef ecosystem [Gil, M.A., Baskett, M.L., Munch, S.B., Hein, A.M., PNAS 117(41), 25580-25589, 2020]. We first show that the underlying demographic model can be reframed naturally as a singularly perturbed system with two fast variables and one slow variable in which bistability can occur in ecologically relevant parameter regimes. We explore the potential for canard-type dynamics in the model, complementing numerical results with an analytical description through the lens of geometric singular perturbation theory, and we describe R-tipping as a result of an increase in the fishing effort. We show that trajectories will undergo canard-induced tipping by passage through a folded node singularity, whereas a folded focus may give rise to tipping of jump type; in both scenarios, a catastrophic collapse occurs in the populations of herbivorous fish and coral, with the population of algae experiencing a ``bloom". Alternatively, we may observe ``tracking" of a sustainable coexistence state between the three populations in the presence of a folded focus.
tldr: This paper studies rate-induced tipping in a coral reef ecosystem using geometric singular perturbation theory, focusing on canard dynamics and folded singularities.
motivation: To understand how slow increases in fishing effort can cause sudden collapse of coral reef ecosystems, beyond classical bifurcation thresholds.
method: The authors reframe a behavioral-demographic model as a singularly perturbed system with two fast and one slow variable, then apply geometric singular perturbation theory and numerical simulations to analyze canard-induced tipping and folded node/focus dynamics.
result: They identify two tipping scenarios: canard-induced tipping via a folded node and jump-type tipping via a folded focus, both leading to collapse of herbivorous fish and coral with algal blooms, while tracking of a sustainable state is possible under certain conditions.
conclusion: The work demonstrates that rate-induced tipping can occur in ecological models due to anthropogenic stress, highlighting the importance of considering rate-dependent thresholds in ecosystem management.

title: Spectral Distribution Of Jacobi Weighted Histopolation Matrices Via Glt Theory
authors: Allal Guessab, Federico Nudo, Stefano Serra-Capizzano
abstract: ArXiv:2605.23501v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper we study a weighted histopolation problem on [MATH] associated with Jacobi weights. In the first part of the present work we prove results in approximation theory, while in the second we analyze the resulting matrices from an asymptotic linear algebra perspective. More in detail, in the first part, given weighted cell averages, we construct a reconstruction operator based on weighted primitives of Jacobi polynomials and investigate the resulting discretization matrices. At any fixed discretization level, we derive an exact factorization of the histopolation matrix through a backward-difference operator and a sampling operator of Jacobi weighted primitives. Combining a sharp integration by parts identity with the three-term recurrence of Jacobi polynomials, we further show that the primitive sampling operator admits an explicit decomposition involving a tridiagonal coupling matrix in the Jacobi spectral index. This yields a tridiagonal factor representation of the histopolation matrix. In the second part, under standard mesh-regularity assumptions, we show that all the various induced matrix sequences belong to the Generalized Locally Toeplitz (GLT) class, by describing in detail the related GLT symbols. As a consequence, we provide the corresponding spectral distributions and discuss their implications for numerical stability when solving the associated linear systems.
tldr: This paper studies spectral distributions of matrices arising from a weighted histopolation problem with Jacobi weights, using GLT theory.
motivation: To understand the asymptotic spectral behavior of discretization matrices from weighted histopolation, which is important for numerical stability.
method: Constructs a reconstruction operator based on weighted primitives of Jacobi polynomials, derives exact factorization of the histopolation matrix, and uses GLT theory to analyze spectral distributions.
result: Shows that the matrix sequences belong to the GLT class and provides explicit GLT symbols, leading to spectral distribution results.
conclusion: The findings have implications for numerical stability when solving linear systems arising from such discretizations.

title: On The Treatment Of Topology Changes On 3d Polyhedral Moving Meshes Via 4d Space-time Hole-like Elements In Direct Ale Ader-dg Methods
authors: Elena Gaburro, Matej Klima, Mauro Bonafini, Maurizio Tavelli
abstract: ArXiv:2605.23506v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This work investigates a novel approach for the high order evolution of hyperbolic PDEs using ADER discontinuous Galerkin schemes within a direct Arbitrary-Lagrangian-Eulerian (ALE) framework on 3D moving polyhedral meshes with topology changes. Our direct ALE method is based on the PDE integration over 4D (3D+time) space-time control volumes connecting the elements of two subsequent tessellations, so to simultaneously evolve the solution both in time and between the two different meshes in an effective and high order manner. In this way, we also avoid any complex and expensive projection-reconstruction techniques and any mesh intersection operation typical of indirect ALE schemes. The crucial step consists in the strategy for building space-time control volumes that also connect elements with different shapes and neighborhoods due to a change in topology. In fact, simply linking existing elements by collapsing or expanding their edges would leave a "hole" in the space-time domain. To fill it, we introduce additional degenerate elements that we call hole-like elements. These are 4D objects with zero 3D volume at both the beginning and end of the timestep, but which possess a strictly non-zero 4D space-time volume. Given the uniqueness of this space-time approach in 3D+time and the necessity of characterizing the geometry of such elements, the main objective of this paper is the formal geometrical and numerical description of the method as well as the presentation of new and intuitive visualization strategies. In particular, we provide a detailed characterization of the hole-like elements arising in correspondence to 2-3, 3-2, and 4-4 flips on the underlying Delaunay tetrahedralization. Finally, we numerically show that the method is fully conservative, satisfies the GCL and maintains the correct order of convergence even in the presence of frequent topology changes.
tldr: This paper presents a novel 4D space-time approach for handling topology changes in 3D moving polyhedral meshes within a direct ALE ADER-DG framework for hyperbolic PDEs.
motivation: To enable high-order evolution of hyperbolic PDEs on moving meshes with topology changes without complex projection-reconstruction or mesh intersection operations.
method: The method uses 4D space-time control volumes connecting elements of two successive tessellations, introducing degenerate 'hole-like' elements to fill gaps caused by topology changes (e.g., 2-3, 3-2, 4-4 flips).
result: The method is fully conservative, satisfies the geometric conservation law (GCL), and maintains correct order of convergence even with frequent topology changes.
conclusion: The approach provides a robust and efficient way to handle topology changes in moving mesh simulations, with potential applications in computational fluid dynamics and other fields requiring adaptive meshing.

title: End-to-End Pseudo-Measurement Learning For State Estimation Under Limited Observability
authors: J. G. de la Varga, S. Pineda, A. Stratigakos, J. M. Morales
abstract: ArXiv:2605.23525v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Distribution System State Estimation (DSSE) is becoming increasingly important with the integration of Distributed Energy Resources (DERs) and the active operation of distribution networks (DNs), but it remains challenging due to the limited and heterogeneous monitoring infrastructure available in these networks. To address this challenge, this paper proposes a novel DSSE framework that restores observability through data-driven pseudo-measurements generated by a Neural Network (NN), while preserving the exact non-linear AC power flow model within a classical Weighted Least Squares (WLS) estimator. Unlike conventional approaches that generate pseudo-measurements independently of the physical estimation process, the proposed method explicitly couples both components through an end-to-end learning formulation. Specifically, the WLS estimator is embedded as a layer within the NN architecture, enabling implicit differentiation to propagate the impact of pseudo-measurements on the final estimation error back to the NN parameters. Extensive numerical experiments on the IEEE 30-bus and IEEE 33-bus systems demonstrate that the proposed framework consistently outperforms state-of-the-art methods in state estimation (SE) accuracy under a wide range of loading conditions and measurement configurations.
tldr: This paper proposes an end-to-end learning framework for distribution system state estimation using neural network-generated pseudo-measurements, but it is unrelated to the user's research interests in quantum information, thermodynamics, or foundations.
motivation: Distribution system state estimation is challenging due to limited monitoring infrastructure, and conventional pseudo-measurement methods are decoupled from the physical estimation process.
method: The authors embed a Weighted Least Squares estimator as a layer in a neural network, enabling end-to-end training via implicit differentiation to optimize pseudo-measurement generation for state estimation accuracy.
result: The proposed framework outperforms state-of-the-art methods on IEEE 30-bus and 33-bus systems under various loading and measurement configurations.
conclusion: The approach improves state estimation accuracy in distribution networks, but its relevance to quantum computing or information thermodynamics is negligible.

title: Accelerating An Ensemble Of Variational Data Assimilations With Randomized Preconditioning
authors: I. Dau\v{z}ickait\.e, S. G\"urol, M. Destouches, L. Berre, A. T. Weaver
abstract: ArXiv:2605.23571v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Ensembles of variational data assimilations (EDA) require solving systems of linear equations with iterative methods. The solution process can be accelerated using a limited memory preconditioner constructed with approximations of the leading eigenpairs of the Hessian matrix. Randomized methods for low-rank matrix approximations provide a feasible approach for computing these eigenpairs. These methods use a random sketching matrix to obtain a low-rank representation of the Hessian matrix, which is then used for computing the eigendecomposition. The sketching matrix highly influences the quality of the approximation. In this paper, we show how the structure of the EDA can be exploited to construct a suitable sketching matrix, i.e., using the differences of the right-hand sides of the linear systems of equations. Idealised numerical experiments with the Lorenz-96 model show that the resulting preconditioner is able to accelerate the EDA solution process for all ensemble members, even if constructed from the control member only.
tldr: This paper proposes a randomized preconditioning method to accelerate ensemble variational data assimilation, using differences of right-hand sides to construct sketching matrices.
motivation: Ensemble variational data assimilation requires solving many linear systems; iterative solvers can be slow. The authors aim to accelerate this by constructing a low-rank preconditioner from Hessian eigenpairs approximated via randomized methods.
method: The authors exploit the structure of the EDA to build a sketching matrix from differences of right-hand sides of the linear systems, then use it to compute a low-rank approximation of the Hessian for preconditioning.
result: Numerical experiments with the Lorenz-96 model show that the preconditioner accelerates the EDA solution process for all ensemble members, even when constructed from only the control member.
conclusion: The method improves computational efficiency of EDA, with potential applications in numerical weather prediction. Future work may extend to more complex models and assess robustness.

title: Coupling Optimization Algorithms And Monotone Control Systems: Suboptimal Model Predictive Control As An Operator Splitting Scheme
authors: Till Preuster, Hannes Gernandt, Manuel Schaller
abstract: ArXiv:2605.23581v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We propose a framework for suboptimal model predictive control (MPC) based on the interconnection of monotone dynamical systems, such as port-Hamiltonian systems. In contrast to classical MPC formulations, where the optimizer is treated as an instantaneous mapping, we model both the plant and the optimizer as dynamical systems and couple them through a structured interconnection. This leads to a continuous-time closed-loop formulation governed by (quasi-)monotone operators. Within this setting, we establish well-posedness of the coupled optimizer-plant dynamics and provide a unified interpretation of suboptimal MPC schemes. In particular, we reveal a direct connection between iterative optimization algorithms and dynamical control systems theory by showing that standard suboptimal MPC algorithms can be understood as time discretizations of the underlying continuous-time dynamics via operator splitting methods.
tldr: This paper proposes a framework for suboptimal model predictive control by coupling monotone dynamical systems and interpreting optimization algorithms as operator splitting schemes.
motivation: To unify suboptimal MPC schemes and provide a continuous-time closed-loop formulation that bridges iterative optimization and dynamical control systems.
method: The authors model both the plant and optimizer as dynamical systems with (quasi-)monotone operators, establish well-posedness, and show that standard suboptimal MPC algorithms correspond to time discretizations via operator splitting.
result: A unified interpretation of suboptimal MPC as interconnected monotone systems, with connections to operator splitting methods.
conclusion: The framework offers a new perspective on MPC but is primarily focused on control theory, with no direct link to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Linear Quadratic Optimal Transport And Interpolation Inequalities
authors: Alec Jacopo Almo Schiavoni Piazza Luca Rizzi
abstract: ArXiv:2605.23608v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper investigates the optimal transport problem within the framework of Linear Quadratic optimal control systems. We establish the well-posedness of the Monge problem and analyze the regularity of the resulting optimal transport map, extending the results obtained in [Hindawi, Pomet, Rifford, 2011] for non-negative costs. Furthermore, we study the displacement interpolation of measures and derive general interpolation inequalities for entropy functionals. Our analysis is motivated by the role of these systems as natural model spaces for comparison theory in sub-Riemannian geometry.
tldr: This paper studies optimal transport in linear quadratic control systems and derives interpolation inequalities for entropy functionals, with applications in sub-Riemannian geometry.
motivation: To extend optimal transport theory to linear quadratic control systems and establish well-posedness and regularity results for the Monge problem.
method: The authors analyze the Monge problem for linear quadratic optimal control systems, study displacement interpolation of measures, and derive interpolation inequalities for entropy functionals.
result: Well-posedness of the Monge problem and regularity of the optimal transport map are established, along with general interpolation inequalities for entropy functionals.
conclusion: The results provide model spaces for comparison theory in sub-Riemannian geometry, but the paper is purely mathematical and not directly connected to the user's research interests.

title: A Non-Iterative Algorithm For Clearing Two-Layer Energy-Sharing Markets With Voltage Constraints
authors: Tonghua Liu, Yifan Su, Zhaojian Wang, Feng Liu
abstract: ArXiv:2605.23671v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Real-time hierarchical energy-sharing markets are promising to coordinate large numbers of prosumers. Still, most existing clearing methods rely on linearized or DC power-flow models and do not explicitly handle reactive power or voltage-security constraints. With AC network constraints, the problem becomes a large-scale bilevel Mathematical Program with Equilibrium Constraints (MPEC) that is difficult to solve in real time. This paper develops a non-iterative clearing algorithm for two-layer energy-sharing markets with voltage constraints. We first derive an efficient best-response function for each lower-layer energy-sharing market and reduce the equilibrium search to one dimension by exploiting the pricing-coupling structure. We then embed this function into the upper-layer network-constrained problem and reformulate the bilevel MPEC as a single-level mixed-integer second-order cone program (MISOCP), which is computationally tractable. Case studies on the IEEE 123-bus system with 12,300 prosumers show that the proposed method preserves nodal voltages within prescribed limits and delivers solutions with maximum errors below 0.01\% in 0.829 s.
tldr: This paper proposes a non-iterative algorithm for clearing two-layer energy-sharing markets with AC voltage constraints, using a bilevel MPEC reformulated as a MISOCP.
motivation: Existing market clearing methods often ignore reactive power and voltage constraints, and solving the resulting bilevel MPEC in real time is challenging.
method: The authors derive a best-response function for lower-layer markets, reduce the equilibrium search to one dimension, and reformulate the bilevel MPEC as a single-level MISOCP.
result: The algorithm solves the IEEE 123-bus system with 12,300 prosumers in 0.829 s with maximum errors below 0.01%, maintaining voltage limits.
conclusion: The method enables real-time clearing of hierarchical energy markets with AC network constraints, but its applicability to quantum or information thermodynamics is not discussed.

title: Concentration Of Measure-valued Solutions For Semilinear Parabolic Equations
authors: Charlie Lebarb\'e (LAAS), \'emilien Flayac (LAAS), Michel Fourni\'e (LAAS), Didier Henrion (LAAS), Milan Korda
abstract: ArXiv:2605.23678v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The moment-sum-of-squares hierarchy provides a powerful framework for solving non-convex optimal control problems by constructing a sequence of convex semidefinite relaxations. However, when extending these methods to nonlinear partial differential equations (PDEs), a fundamental challenge is the potential existence of a relaxation gap, where the solution to the linear measure formulation using occupation measures fails to correspond to a classical physical solution of the original PDE. In this paper, we prove the absence of a relaxation gap for scalar semilinear parabolic PDEs of the reaction-diffusion type. We do so by showing that each solution to the linear measure equation gives rise to an energy measure-valued (emv) solution in the space of Young measures satisfying suitable energy identities. We then prove that any such emv solution concentrates on the solution to the nonlinear PDE, provided the latter exists and is unique. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first concentration result of this kind for measure-valued solutions of reaction-diffusion PDEs.
tldr: This paper proves that measure-valued solutions to semilinear parabolic PDEs concentrate on classical solutions, closing the relaxation gap for moment-sum-of-squares hierarchies in optimal control of reaction-diffusion PDEs.
motivation: To address the fundamental challenge of relaxation gaps when using moment-sum-of-squares hierarchies for nonlinear PDE optimal control, ensuring that the linear measure formulation yields physically meaningful solutions.
method: The authors introduce energy measure-valued (emv) solutions in the space of Young measures and show that any solution to the linear measure equation gives rise to an emv solution satisfying energy identities. They then prove concentration of emv solutions onto the unique classical solution of the nonlinear PDE.
result: The paper proves the absence of a relaxation gap for scalar semilinear parabolic PDEs of reaction-diffusion type, establishing that measure-valued solutions concentrate on the unique classical solution when it exists.
conclusion: This result validates the use of moment-sum-of-squares hierarchies for optimal control of reaction-diffusion PDEs, with potential extensions to broader classes of nonlinear PDEs.

title: An Axiomatic Theory Of Tie-Breaking: Impossibility, Characterization, And Decomposition
authors: Frank M. V. Feys
abstract: ArXiv:2605.22846v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop an abstract axiomatic theory of tie-breaking. A tie-breaking input consists of a finite set N of players, a weak order on N representing the standings to be refined, and an auxiliary information item drawn from a set on which the symmetric group Sym(N) acts. Within this minimal framework we prove three theorems. First, no tie-breaking rule producing a strict linear order can be anonymous, provided the input space contains even one intrinsically symmetric situation, a condition met in essentially every realistic application. Second, when we allow the rule to output a partition of N (rather than a strict ranking), there is a unique rule satisfying two natural axioms: it is the partition of N into orbits of the joint stabilizer of the input. Third, every reasonable strict tie-breaking rule decomposes uniquely as the canonical orbit partition followed by an arbitrary completion. The decomposition makes precise the informal observation that real tie-breaking systems are honest until forced to be arbitrary. The framework is broad enough to capture chess tournament tie-breakers, sports league regulations, voting tie-breakers, tie-breaking among symmetric players in cooperative games, and ranking by network centrality measures, all within a single uniform formalism.
tldr: This paper develops an axiomatic theory of tie-breaking rules, proving impossibility results and a unique decomposition, but it is unrelated to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: To provide a formal framework for understanding tie-breaking in various contexts such as sports, voting, and cooperative games.
method: Axiomatic approach using group actions and symmetry, proving theorems about anonymity and decomposition.
result: No anonymous tie-breaking rule can produce a strict linear order; the unique rule outputting a partition is the orbit partition; any strict rule decomposes into orbit partition plus arbitrary completion.
conclusion: The framework unifies many real-world tie-breaking systems and clarifies the role of symmetry and arbitrariness.

title: The Geometry Of Cooperative Game Solutions: Stratified Egalitarian Shapley Values
authors: Frank M. V. Feys
abstract: ArXiv:2605.22847v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The space L of linear value maps on a finite-player cooperative game G^N is finite-dimensional, and admits a canonical inner product induced by the Harsanyi-dividend decomposition of G^N. We show that this inner product is intrinsic: the same value arises from any orthonormal basis of G^N with respect to the Harsanyi inner product. Within this geometry, the subspace L^{ESL} of efficient, symmetric, linear value maps admits a clean structure theorem. The induced orthogonal stratification of L by coalition size yields a canonical linear isomorphism L^{ESL} = R^{n-1}, under which every efficient symmetric linear value map decomposes uniquely into n-1 stratified epsilons, one per coalition size. The classical egalitarian Shapley family of Joosten (1996) is precisely the diagonal slice of this R^{n-1}. The orthogonal projection of any Psi in L^{ESL} onto this diagonal yields an optimal parameter eps*(Psi) equal to the weighted mean of the stratified epsilons under an explicit probability distribution {w_a} over coalition sizes, and the goodness-of-fit R^2(Psi) equals one minus the relative weighted variance of those epsilons. The framework is a literal regression-statistics analogue of the coefficient of determination. At n=4 it produces a clean three-way classification of the standard alternatives to the Shapley value: the Banzhaf value is nearly orthogonal to the egalitarian Shapley axis (R^2 ~ 1%); the equal-surplus-division value is moderately aligned (R^2 ~ 38%); the solidarity value is almost entirely aligned (R^2 ~ 99.6%). Asymptotically R^2(ESD) -> 1, R^2(So) -> 1, and R^2(Bz) -> 1/2, the last reflecting a structural identity between the efficiency defect and the egalitarian-Shapley deviation of the Banzhaf value at every coalition size.
tldr: This paper develops a geometric framework for cooperative game solutions, introducing stratified egalitarian Shapley values and analyzing their alignment with classical values via regression statistics.
motivation: To provide a unified geometric perspective on cooperative game solutions and quantify the relationship between different value concepts.
method: The authors define an inner product on the space of linear value maps using the Harsanyi dividend decomposition, then study the subspace of efficient symmetric linear maps and its orthogonal stratification by coalition size.
result: They show that the egalitarian Shapley family corresponds to a diagonal slice, and compute the orthogonal projection and R^2 for Banzhaf, equal-surplus-division, and solidarity values, revealing varying degrees of alignment.
conclusion: The framework offers a regression-statistics analogue for comparing cooperative game solutions, with potential applications in understanding value selection and axiomatic properties.

title: PrefBench: Evaluating Zero-Shot Llm Agents In Hidden-Preference Personalized Pricing Negotiations
authors: Yingjie Lei
abstract: ArXiv:2605.22855v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Personalized pricing negotiations are a challenging testbed for LLM agents because successful interaction does not guarantee profitable decision making. A seller may produce valid actions and close many deals while still pricing poorly when buyer willingness to pay and bargaining traits remain hidden. This paper presents PrefBench, a simulator-based benchmark for hidden-preference personalized pricing negotiations. Each episode pairs a simulated buyer with a fixed vehicle-customization bundle; the seller observes public persona descriptors, bundle information, and negotiation history, while latent buyer variables govern valuation, patience, counter-offer behavior, and walkaway decisions. PrefBench evaluates this setting through an LLM-facing state-summary protocol that constrains agents to return strict JSON actions under a fixed hidden-information boundary. We evaluate zero-shot LLM sellers against heuristic references over 7,500 episodes. The tested LLMs follow the protocol reliably and achieve deal rates above 0.99, but their seller-profit outcomes remain weak: the best LLM average profit is only slightly above the random baseline and far below a simple concession heuristic under the same episode stream. These results show that structured action compliance and agreement-seeking behavior can coexist with weak profit-sensitive bargaining. PrefBench provides a controlled benchmark for evaluating pricing-agent behavior under hidden buyer preferences.
tldr: This paper introduces a benchmark for evaluating zero-shot LLM agents in hidden-preference personalized pricing negotiations, finding that LLMs achieve high deal rates but poor profit performance.
motivation: To assess whether LLM agents can make profitable decisions in personalized pricing negotiations where buyer preferences are hidden, a challenging testbed for AI.
method: The authors built PrefBench, a simulator with a state-summary protocol that constrains LLM agents to output JSON actions, and tested zero-shot LLM sellers against heuristic baselines over 7,500 episodes.
result: LLMs reliably followed the protocol and achieved deal rates above 0.99, but their average profit was only slightly above random and far below a simple concession heuristic.
conclusion: Structured action compliance and agreement-seeking behavior can coexist with weak profit-sensitive bargaining; PrefBench provides a controlled benchmark for further research.

title: Multi-Dimensional Matching In Market Design
authors: Irene Aldridge
abstract: ArXiv:2605.22865v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper proposes a computationally efficient mechanism for multi-dimensional matching markets where agents report preferences over object features rather than complete utility assessments. We use Singular Value Decomposition (SVD) to identify the principal direction of variation in feature space and match agents to objects along this dimension, reducing a complex multi-dimensional problem to an effectively one-dimensional problem solvable in [MATH] time. We show that when data exhibit low effective dimensionality, our mechanism approximately maximizes Nash Social Welfare, satisfies distributional truthfulness, and achieves symmetry. We establish a novel connection between Nash Social Welfare and Geometric Distributionally Robust Optimization, providing robustness guaranties. Numerical experiments demonstrate that our approach achieves 99\% optimal welfare while running three orders of magnitude faster than direct optimization. The framework applies naturally to school choice, labor markets, and course allocation, where feature-based elicitation reduces the cognitive burden on agents.
tldr: This paper proposes a computationally efficient mechanism for multi-dimensional matching markets using SVD to reduce dimensionality and approximately maximize Nash Social Welfare.
motivation: To design a scalable matching mechanism that reduces cognitive burden on agents by eliciting preferences over features rather than full utilities.
method: Uses Singular Value Decomposition to identify principal variation direction, reducing multi-dimensional matching to a one-dimensional problem solvable in O(n log n) time.
result: The mechanism achieves 99% optimal welfare while running three orders of magnitude faster than direct optimization, and satisfies distributional truthfulness and symmetry.
conclusion: The framework applies to school choice, labor markets, and course allocation, with potential for further robustness guarantees via geometric distributionally robust optimization.

title: Query Lower Bounds For Correlation Clustering Under Memory Constraints
authors: Sumegha Garg, Songhua He, Periklis A. Papakonstantinou
abstract: ArXiv:2605.23104v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This work initiates the study of memory-query tradeoffs for graph problems, with a focus on correlation clustering. Correlation clustering asks for a partition of the vertices that minimizes disagreements: non-edges inside clusters plus edges across clusters. Our first result is a tight query lower bound: to output a partition whose cost approximates the optimum up to an additive error of [MATH], any algorithm requires [MATH] adjacency-matrix queries. Under memory constraints, we show that even for the seemingly easier task of approximating the optimal clustering cost (without producing a partition), any algorithm in the random query model must make [MATH] adjacency-matrix queries. Finally, we prove the first general graph model query lower bound for correlation clustering, where algorithms are allowed adjacency-matrix, neighbor, and degree queries. The latter two bounds are not yet tight, leaving room for sharper results.
tldr: This paper studies query lower bounds for correlation clustering under memory constraints, a topic in theoretical computer science with no direct connection to the user's research interests.
motivation: To understand the fundamental tradeoffs between memory and queries for graph problems, specifically correlation clustering.
method: The authors prove lower bounds using information-theoretic arguments and adversarial strategies in various query models (adjacency-matrix, random query, general graph model).
result: Tight query lower bound for additive approximation of correlation clustering; memory-constrained lower bounds for approximating optimal cost; first general graph model lower bound for correlation clustering.
conclusion: The results establish fundamental limits for correlation clustering under memory constraints, but the bounds are not yet tight in all models, leaving open questions for future work.

title: What Does The Server See? Understanding Privacy Leakage From Large Language Models In Split Inference
authors: Mingyuan Fan, Yu Liu, Fuyi Wang, Cen Chen
abstract: ArXiv:2605.23158v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The deployment of large language models (LLMs) on resource-constrained devices remains challenging, spurring interest in split inference, where models are partitioned between client and server to reduce computational burden and enhance privacy by transmitting only intermediate activations. However, the privacy-preserving capabilities of split inference, particularly in the context of LLMs, have not been exhaustively investigated. To fill this gap, we introduce ActInv, which solves an intermediate activation matching problem to reconstruct the client's input. Extensive evaluations demonstrate that ActInv achieves high-fidelity reconstructions, even in the presence of common perturbation-based defenses such as Gaussian noise injection and activation sparsification. To systematically understand this vulnerability, we develop Perturbation Amplification Factor (PAF), a metric for quantifying a layer's inherent resistance to reconstruction. Our analysis reveals that privacy vulnerability is not uniform across layers, with some layers being highly susceptible to leakage while others offer natural resistance. Furthermore, we demonstrate that defense effectiveness can be significantly improved by calibrating perturbation directions to maximize reconstruction error during backpropagation. Building on these insights, we design PriPert and conduct comprehensive evaluations, covering privacy, utility, and computational overhead, to demonstrate its effectiveness.
tldr: This paper investigates privacy leakage in split inference for large language models, proposing an attack method and a defense, but is unrelated to the user's research interests in quantum information and thermodynamics.
motivation: To address the lack of understanding of privacy risks in split inference for LLMs, where intermediate activations are transmitted.
method: Introduces ActInv, which solves an intermediate activation matching problem to reconstruct client input, and develops Perturbation Amplification Factor (PAF) to quantify layer vulnerability.
result: ActInv achieves high-fidelity reconstructions even with perturbation defenses; privacy vulnerability varies across layers.
conclusion: Defenses can be improved by calibrating perturbation directions; proposes PriPert defense with evaluation.

title: Robust Llm Watermarking With Minimal Semantic Distortion For Ip Protection
authors: Kieu Dang, Phung Lai, Nhathai Phan, Yelong Shen, Ruoming Jin
abstract: ArXiv:2605.23175v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Proprietary large language models (LLMs) face risks of intellectual property (IP) violation, as adversaries can replicate an LLM by collecting input-output pairs to train a surrogate model, causing financial setbacks. Watermarks offer a promising defense to verify ownership, but existing methods often struggle with semantic distortion, factual inconsistency, and adversarial attacks. In addition, key-conditioned watermarks for provider-specific detection, especially in cross-provider and multi-user scenarios, remain largely underexplored. To address these challenges, we propose SAFESEAL, a novel key-conditioned watermarking framework that achieves strong detectability with minimal impact on model utility, effectively balancing detectability, utility, and robustness. SAFESEAL preserves named entities while substituting linguistic terms with context-aware synonyms through a key-conditioned Tournament sampling mechanism, maintaining semantic fidelity and factual consistency. For detection, we introduce a key-conditioned contrastive detector that jointly encodes the text and key, enabling provider-specific and robust watermark verification. We derive theoretical bounds on the utility-detectability trade-off and significantly reduce latency through lightweight models, batching, and parallelism. Extensive experiments show that SAFESEAL outperforms baselines in utility, detectability, and robustness, achieving a BERTScore of 0.983, entity similarity of 0.963, a 98.2% detection rate, and the highest human ratings for text quality and content preservation, with latency comparable to the fastest baseline. To promote transparency and community-driven progress, we release the first public watermark leaderboard and an interactive demo.
tldr: This paper proposes a key-conditioned watermarking framework for LLMs to protect intellectual property, focusing on semantic fidelity and robustness against attacks.
motivation: Proprietary LLMs face IP violation risks from adversaries training surrogate models; existing watermarks suffer from semantic distortion and lack provider-specific detection.
method: SAFESEAL uses key-conditioned Tournament sampling to replace linguistic terms with context-aware synonyms while preserving named entities, and a contrastive detector for robust verification.
result: Achieves BERTScore 0.983, entity similarity 0.963, 98.2% detection rate, and high human ratings, with latency comparable to fastest baselines.
conclusion: The framework balances detectability, utility, and robustness, and the authors release a public leaderboard and demo for community progress.

title: Are Frontier LLMs Ready For Cybersecurity? Evidence For Vertical Foundation Models From Dual-Mode Vulnerability Benchmarks
authors: Vivek Dahiya, Sunny Nehra, Vipul Dholariya, Bhavik Shangari, Chandra Khatri
abstract: ArXiv:2605.23243v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We evaluate whether frontier LLMs are ready for cybersecurity through a dual-mode benchmark: white-box function-level vulnerability detection (VulnLLM-R, across C/Java/Python) and black-box web application security testing (five production-style applications with 118 ground-truth vulnerabilities across 20+ CWE families, which we will open-source). We test six frontier models (GPT-5.4, Codex~5.3, Claude Opus~4.6, Sonnet~4.6, Gemini~3.1~Pro and Gemini~3~Flash) and two domain-specialized models across four testing paradigms. Our findings are sobering: (1)~every frontier model produces 10-50% false positive rates in white-box detection, systematically over-predicting vulnerabilities; (2)~in black-box testing, frontier models achieve only 4-8% ground-truth coverage, improving to just 10-19% even with external security tools (Playwright MCP, Burp Suite MCP); (3)~structured penetration-testing methodology encoded in domain-specialized agents raises per-family detection above 50%, demonstrating that methodology, not scale, is the primary lever; and (4)~a domain-specialized defense model achieves the highest precision (0.904) and lowest false positive rate (9.7%) among all models, on a single GPU. We identify the absence of structured security testing traces end-to-end request/response sequences, failure-heavy data, and multi-step attack chains as the fundamental training data bottleneck, and propose self-play security testing as a data generation strategy. Our results make the case for vertical foundation models purpose-built for cybersecurity.
tldr: This paper evaluates frontier LLMs on cybersecurity vulnerability detection and finds they perform poorly, advocating for domain-specialized models.
motivation: To assess whether general-purpose LLMs are ready for practical cybersecurity tasks and to identify bottlenecks.
method: Dual-mode benchmark: white-box function-level vulnerability detection across C/Java/Python and black-box web application security testing with 118 vulnerabilities.
result: Frontier LLMs have high false positive rates (10-50%) in white-box tests and low ground-truth coverage (4-8%) in black-box tests; domain-specialized models with structured methodology achieve >50% detection.
conclusion: Current LLMs are not ready for cybersecurity; vertical foundation models with structured testing traces are needed.

title: Formal Verification Of Probing Security Via Conditional Independence
authors: Katsuyuki Takashima Satoshi Kura
abstract: ArXiv:2605.23316v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Side-channel attacks are a major threat to the security of cryptosystems. Masking is a widely used countermeasure against such attacks, but proving the security of masked algorithms is error-prone without formal verification. In this work, we propose a novel approach to formal verification of noninterference properties of masked algorithms based on probabilistic separation logic. By establishing a connection between noninterference and conditional independence, we show how noninterference can be verified using Lilac, a separation logic for conditional independence. We also provide several proof rules that facilitate the verification of probing security and demonstrate their application to example algorithms.
tldr: This paper proposes a formal verification method for probing security of masked algorithms using probabilistic separation logic and conditional independence.
motivation: Side-channel attacks threaten cryptosystems, and proving security of masked algorithms manually is error-prone, motivating automated formal verification.
method: The authors connect noninterference to conditional independence and use Lilac, a separation logic for conditional independence, to verify probing security, providing proof rules.
result: They demonstrate the approach on example algorithms, showing that conditional independence can effectively verify noninterference properties.
conclusion: The work provides a novel formal verification framework for masked algorithms, but its relevance to quantum information or thermodynamics is minimal.

title: On The Approximate Non-Deterministic Degree Of Total Boolean Functions
authors: Supartha Podder Samruddhi Pednekar
abstract: ArXiv:2605.23336v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The approximate non-deterministic degree of a Boolean function [MATH], denoted [MATH] (written [MATH] for brevity), is the minimum degree of a real polynomial [MATH] such that [MATH] whenever [MATH], and [MATH] whenever [MATH]. Unlike exact non-deterministic degree, which only requires the polynomial to be nonzero on [MATH]-inputs, this measure enforces a uniform gap: the polynomial must stay close to zero on all [MATH]-inputs and bounded away from zero on all [MATH]-inputs. The rational degree conjecture, open for over three decades, was recently resolved by Kothari, Kovacs-Deak, Wang, and Yang, who showed that for every total Boolean function [MATH], \[ deg(f) \le \widetilde O\!\left((f)^3\right). \] In their paper, they explicitly propose a stronger conjecture: that approximate degree is polynomially bounded by [MATH] and [MATH] jointly, i.e., for every total Boolean function [MATH] and every constant [MATH], \[ (f) \le (\mathsf N_{\epsilon}(f), \mathsf N_{\epsilon}(\overline f)). \] This conjecture, if true, would imply a polynomial version of the rational degree result and bring us closer to resolving de Wolf's longstanding non-deterministic degree conjecture. In this work, we make the first systematic progress on this problem, establishing the conjecture for several broad and natural function classes: monotone and unate functions, functions of bounded alternation number, symmetric functions, [MATH]-uniform hypergraph properties, and read-[MATH] Disjunctive Normal Form (DNF) formulas.
tldr: This paper proves a conjecture relating approximate non-deterministic degree to non-deterministic degree for several classes of Boolean functions, advancing complexity theory but not directly connected to the user's research interests.
motivation: To resolve a stronger conjecture proposed by Kothari et al. that approximate degree is polynomially bounded by non-deterministic degree and its complement, which would imply a polynomial version of the rational degree result.
method: The authors systematically analyze specific function classes (monotone, unate, bounded alternation, symmetric, hypergraph properties, read-once DNF) and prove the conjecture for each using combinatorial and algebraic arguments.
result: The conjecture holds for all considered function classes, providing the first systematic progress on the problem.
conclusion: The results bring us closer to resolving de Wolf's non-deterministic degree conjecture, but the paper is purely theoretical in computational complexity and does not address quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Beyond The Half-Approximation: Fair And Efficient Online Class Matching
authors: Max Springer Sander Borst
abstract: ArXiv:2605.23408v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Online bipartite matching, where agents are known in advance but items arrive sequentially and must be irrevocably assigned, is fundamental to problems ranging from ride-sharing to online advertising. When agents belong to classes such as demographic groups or geographic regions, fairness demands equitable treatment across these groups. Recent work introduced class envy-freeness (CEF), a natural extension of the classical fair division notion: an algorithm is [MATH]-CEF if each class receives value at least an [MATH] fraction of what it could extract from any other class's bundle. However, all known algorithms achieving constant-factor CEF guarantees attain utilitarian social welfare (total matching value) of at most [MATH] times the optimum, far below the [MATH] achievable without fairness constraints. We resolve the open question of whether fairness necessitates this efficiency loss, by introducing threshold-based algorithms parameterized by [MATH] that equalize allocations across classes until threshold [MATH], then maximize efficiency. For divisible matching, this yields simultaneous [MATH]-CEF and [MATH]-USW guarantees; for indivisible matching, [MATH]-CEF with the same USW. Setting [MATH] produces the first algorithms beating [MATH]-USW while maintaining constant CEF. We complement this with a novel upper bound construction, proving no non-wasteful [MATH]-CEF algorithm can exceed [MATH]-USW and correcting prior bounds that were vacuous for [MATH]. Our upper bound nearly matches our algorithms' performance, giving the first substantive characterization of the price of fairness in online class matching.
tldr: This paper studies fair and efficient online bipartite matching with class envy-freeness, achieving improved trade-offs between fairness and utilitarian social welfare.
motivation: To resolve whether fairness constraints necessarily cause significant efficiency loss in online class matching, and to provide algorithms that beat the known half-approximation barrier.
method: Introduces threshold-based algorithms that equalize allocations across classes up to a threshold, then maximize efficiency; also provides upper bound constructions.
result: Achieves simultaneous constant CEF and improved USW guarantees (e.g., 1/2-CEF with 2/3-USW for divisible matching), and proves no non-wasteful algorithm can exceed 2/3-USW.
conclusion: Provides the first substantive characterization of the price of fairness in online class matching, with tight bounds and practical algorithms.

title: An Exact Cooperation Formula For Introspection Dynamics In The Heterogeneous Public Goods Game
authors: Harry Foster, Vincent A. Knight, Sebastian Krapohl
abstract: ArXiv:2605.23513v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Cooperation in heterogeneous groups, where individuals differ in resources, productivity, and behavioural responsiveness, underpins collective action across many social and biological systems. Introspection dynamics, in which each player compares their payoff to what they would have received under the alternative action, provides a natural learning rule for such asymmetric settings. We study introspection dynamics on multiplayer games in which the payoff difference [MATH] evaluated by a player when considering a strategy switch is independent of all other players' current actions, a property we call state-independence. Under this condition the introspection Markov chain decomposes as a random-scan product of [MATH] independent two-state chains, one per player, and the stationary distribution is a product measure. As our main application we consider the heterogeneous public goods game, where [MATH] players may differ in their contributions [MATH], public goods multipliers [MATH], and selection intensities [MATH]. We prove that the linear payoff structure implies state-independence, and the long-run cooperation probability admits the exact closed form $[MATH][MATH]r_i = N$ (under symmetric mutation), payoff-neutrality under zero selection intensity, and the sign of each player's sensitivity to their own parameters.
tldr: This paper derives an exact closed-form formula for cooperation probability in heterogeneous public goods games under introspection dynamics with state-independent payoff differences.
motivation: To understand cooperation in heterogeneous groups where individuals differ in resources and behavior, and to provide analytical results for introspection dynamics in multiplayer games.
method: The authors identify a condition called state-independence under which the introspection Markov chain decomposes into independent two-state chains per player, allowing product stationary distribution. They apply this to the heterogeneous public goods game with linear payoffs.
result: They prove that linear payoff structure implies state-independence, and derive an exact closed-form expression for long-run cooperation probability, showing it equals the product of individual cooperation probabilities under symmetric mutation.
conclusion: The work provides a tractable analytical framework for cooperation in heterogeneous groups, with implications for social and biological collective action, but is not directly related to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Formally Verified Liveness With Multiparty Session Types In Rocq
authors: Omer Keskin, Nobuko Yoshida, Rob van Glabbeek
abstract: ArXiv:2605.23633v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Multiparty session types (MPST) offer a framework for the description of communication-based protocols involving multiple participants. In the top-down approach to MPST, the communication pattern of the session is described using a global type. Then the global type is projected on to a local type for each participant, and the individual processes making up the session are type-checked against these projections. Typed sessions possess certain desirable properties such as safety, deadlock-freedom and liveness. In this work, we present the first mechanised proof of liveness for synchronous multiparty session types in the Rocq Proof Assistant. Building on recent work, we represent global and local types as coinductive trees using the paco library. We use a coinductively defined subtyping relation on local types together with another coinductively defined plain-merge projection relation relating local and global types. We then associate collections of local types, or local type contexts, with global types using this projection and subtyping relations, and prove an operational correspondence between a local type context and its associated global type. We utilise this association relation to prove the safety and liveness of associated local type contexts and, consequently, the multiparty sessions typed by these contexts. Besides clarifying the often informal proofs found in the MPST literature, our Rocq mechanisation also enables the certification of liveness properties of communication protocols. Our contribution amounts to around 14K lines of Rocq code, available at [URL] .
tldr: This paper presents a mechanized proof of liveness for synchronous multiparty session types using the Rocq proof assistant.
motivation: To provide a formal, machine-checked proof of liveness for multiparty session types, which is often only informally argued in the literature.
method: The authors represent global and local types as coinductive trees using the paco library, define coinductive subtyping and projection relations, and prove an operational correspondence between local type contexts and global types.
result: They successfully mechanized the proof of safety and liveness for associated local type contexts, amounting to about 14K lines of Rocq code.
conclusion: The work clarifies informal proofs and enables certification of liveness properties of communication protocols, but is focused on formal verification rather than the user's research interests.

title: Kernel-Based ReLU Approximation For Homomorphic Encryption-Compatible Privacy-preserving Deep Learning Models
authors: Dimitrios Sygletos, Dimitra Papatsaroucha, Marios Choudetsanakis, Ilias Politis, Evangelos K. Markakis
abstract: ArXiv:2605.23641v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: As privacy concerns in AI technologies continue to grow, Homomorphic Encryption (HE) offers a way to perform computations on encrypted data without the need of decryption during operations. However, HE is limited to addition and multiplication, making non-linear functions incompatible in their original form. This limitation has become more critical with the widespread use of Large Language Models (LLMs), where the non-linearity of activation functions such as the Rectified Linear Unit (ReLU) poses challenges for deployment in privacy-preserving Natural Language Processing (NLP) settings. This paper proposes a kernel-based approximation of ReLU, enabling its use within HE-constrained settings and thus contributing a critical step toward supporting privacy-preserving LLMs. A smooth kernel-based function, mimicking ReLU, is approximated using a second-degree polynomial, inspired by Jackson's theorem, to achieve low multiplicative depth. The proposed method is trained and assessed directly on token embeddings from pre-trained LLMs and evaluated in various scenarios, from simulated and tokenized data to deep learning and transformer models. Results show improved approximation fidelity, supporting the method's suitability for secure and privacy-preserving inference in various tasks.
tldr: This paper proposes a kernel-based polynomial approximation of ReLU for use in homomorphic encryption-based privacy-preserving deep learning.
motivation: Homomorphic encryption only supports addition and multiplication, making non-linear activation functions like ReLU incompatible. This limits privacy-preserving deployment of LLMs.
method: A smooth kernel-based function mimicking ReLU is approximated using a second-degree polynomial inspired by Jackson's theorem to achieve low multiplicative depth.
result: The proposed approximation shows improved fidelity compared to existing methods when evaluated on token embeddings from pre-trained LLMs and various deep learning models.
conclusion: The method enables secure and privacy-preserving inference for NLP tasks, contributing to the development of privacy-preserving LLMs.

title: Multi-User Mimo With Rotatable Antennas And Irs: Joint Antenna Boresight And Irs Orientation Design
authors: Guoying Zhang, Qingqing Wu, Ziyuan Zheng, Qiaoyan Peng, Ailing Zheng, Yanze Zhu, Ying Gao, Wen Chen
abstract: ArXiv:2605.23683v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we investigate an intelligent reflecting surface (IRS)-assisted multi-user system, where the base station (BS) employs rotatable antennas (RAs) and the IRS can adjust the panel orientation.To alleviate the severe multiplicative path loss of the cascaded channel, the IRS is deployed near the BS, while the user-BS and user-IRS links remain in the far field. We formulate a sum-rate maximization problem by jointly optimizing the receive beamforming, IRS phase shifts, BS antenna boresights, and IRS panel orientation. To tackle the resulting highly coupled and non-convex problem, we first study a single-user case to reveal the structure of the dual-rotation gain, which is shown to be multiplicatively separable in the far field but coupled in the near field. For the general multi-user case, we develop an alternating optimization algorithm, where the receive beamforming is updated in closed form, the IRS phase shifts are optimized by an FP-assisted Riemannian conjugate gradient method, and the BS antenna boresights and IRS panel orientation are updated via projected gradient methods. Simulation results demonstrate the significant sum-rate gains achieved by the proposed coordinated rotation design over fixed-orientation and single-rotation benchmark schemes, and provide useful insights into near-field dual-rotation design.
tldr: This paper studies IRS-assisted multi-user MIMO with rotatable antennas, focusing on joint optimization of antenna boresights and IRS orientation to maximize sum-rate.
motivation: To overcome multiplicative path loss in IRS cascaded channels by deploying IRS near the BS and using rotatable antennas, and to explore the dual-rotation gain.
method: Formulates a sum-rate maximization problem and solves it via alternating optimization: closed-form beamforming, FP-assisted Riemannian conjugate gradient for IRS phases, and projected gradient for antenna boresights and IRS orientation.
result: The proposed coordinated rotation design achieves significant sum-rate gains over fixed-orientation and single-rotation benchmarks, with insights into near-field dual-rotation coupling.
conclusion: The work demonstrates the benefits of joint antenna and IRS orientation optimization, but is limited to far-field user links and specific deployment assumptions.

title: An ASP-based Approach To Solving General Stochastic Two-Player Games
authors: Michael Thielscher Yifan He
abstract: ArXiv:2605.23705v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Game Description Language (GDL) is a widely used formalism for specifying general games. Due to their similar syntax and semantics, Answer Set Programming (ASP) and its extensions have been applied to single- and two-player deterministic turn-taking GDL games. This paper presents the first ASP-based approach for solving two-player turn-taking GDL games with uncertainty. We introduce Stochastic An- swer Set Programming (SQASP) to encode the maximally achievable winning probability for a given player in stochastic GDL games, and develop a translation-based solver that evaluates SQASP programs by converting them to Extended Stochastic Satisfiability. Our empirical results show that the proposed approach is competitive with forward search on small stochastic games and can potentially support general game players in endgame evaluation.
tldr: This paper presents an ASP-based approach for solving stochastic two-player games, with no direct connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: To extend ASP-based game solving to stochastic games, which are not covered by previous deterministic approaches.
method: Introduces Stochastic Answer Set Programming (SQASP) and translates it to Extended Stochastic Satisfiability for solving.
result: The approach is competitive with forward search on small stochastic games and may aid endgame evaluation.
conclusion: The work provides a new method for stochastic game solving but is not relevant to the user's research interests.

title: Recursion And Proof Theoretical Characterizations Of Small Circuit Classes With Modulo Counting Via Discrete Differential Equations (long Version)
authors: Melissa Antonelli, Arnaud Durand, Rui Li
abstract: ArXiv:2605.23805v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The paper proposes an implicit (i.e., machine-independent) complexity approach to studying computation by polynomial-size, constant-depth circuits with gates counting modulo a constant through the lens of discrete ordinary differential equations (ODEs). So far, recursion-theoretic characterizations have been provided for functions computed by circuits of constant depth, including gates counting modulo 2 and 6 only (i.e., for the classes FAC0[2] and FAC0[6], resp.). In this paper, it is shown that considering ODE schemas, rather than bounded recursion, allows for a more fine-grained analysis, leading to (uniform) characterizations for all classes FAC0[n] (n \in N), i.e. functions computed by circuits including counting modulo n gates. Inspired by the syntactic form of the ODE schemas, we go further in this direction and present first-order bounded theories for capturing provably total functions in each of these classes.
tldr: This paper uses discrete ODEs to characterize circuit complexity classes with modulo counting, but is unrelated to the user's research interests.
motivation: To provide machine-independent characterizations of functions computed by polynomial-size, constant-depth circuits with modulo counting gates, extending previous results for modulo 2 and 6 to all moduli.
method: The authors employ discrete ordinary differential equation (ODE) schemas instead of bounded recursion to achieve a more fine-grained analysis, and develop first-order bounded theories for capturing provably total functions.
result: They obtain uniform characterizations for all classes FAC0[n] (n ∈ N), i.e., functions computed by circuits including counting modulo n gates.
conclusion: The work advances implicit complexity theory for small circuit classes, but has no direct connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: A Blueprint For Constructing 3-pass Ake Protocols Under Commitment-based Models
authors: Rodrigo Mart\'in S\'anchez-Ledesma
abstract: ArXiv:2605.23843v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The commitment-based AKE model provides a formal security framework for key exchange protocols that avoid long-term cryptographic material, achieving authentication through a final out-of-band verification of session-derived values. Within this model, secure KA-based and KEM-based protocols were previously constructed via a commitment-based MT compiler, yielding optimized 4-pass protocols. In this work, we show that 3-pass protocols secure under this model exist for both primitives. These protocols are constructed ad hoc, following the core ideas of the commitment-based MT authenticator, and their SK security in the unauthenticated model is proved using the same game-based techniques, achieving bounds of the same form as those previously achieved. The resulting protocols provide one-way authentication in three message exchanges.
tldr: This paper presents a blueprint for constructing 3-pass authenticated key exchange protocols under commitment-based models, achieving one-way authentication in three message exchanges.
motivation: Previous commitment-based AKE protocols required four passes; the goal was to reduce the number of message exchanges to three while maintaining security.
method: The authors construct ad hoc 3-pass protocols for KA-based and KEM-based primitives, following the core ideas of the commitment-based MT authenticator, and prove SK security using game-based techniques.
result: They show that 3-pass protocols secure under the commitment-based AKE model exist for both KA and KEM primitives, with security bounds of the same form as the 4-pass versions.
conclusion: The work demonstrates that one-way authentication can be achieved in three message exchanges, potentially improving efficiency in key exchange protocols.

title: Leveraging Large Language Models For Sentiment Analysis: Multi-Modal Analysis Of Decentraland's Mana Token
authors: Xintong Wu, Peiting Tsai, Jing Yuan, Michael Yu, Greg Sun, Luyao Zhang
abstract: ArXiv:2605.20192v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Decentraland, a decentralized virtual reality platform operating within the expanding Metaverse ecosystem, utilizes its native MANA token to facilitate virtual asset transactions and governance. This study investigates the integration of Discord community sentiment with multi-modal financial data to enhance cryptocurrency price prediction within virtual world economies. We address: (1) identifying sentiment patterns within Decentraland's Discord community, and (2) evaluating the impact of multi-modal features on token return forecasting. Using a BERT-based large language model for sentiment analysis, we develop two LSTM architectures: a baseline incorporating historical prices and a multi-modal variant integrating sentiment scores, trading volume, and market capitalization. Results indicate predominantly neutral community sentiment with a positive skew. The multi-modal model significantly outperforms the price-only baseline in prediction accuracy. These findings demonstrate the predictive value of community-derived signals for virtual economy forecasting and establish a foundation for future research at the intersection of immersive virtual environments, natural language processing, and cryptocurrency market analysis.
tldr: This paper uses BERT-based sentiment analysis on Discord data to predict MANA token returns, finding that multi-modal features improve prediction over price-only models.
motivation: To explore whether community sentiment from Discord can enhance cryptocurrency price prediction in virtual world economies like Decentraland.
method: A BERT-based LLM extracts sentiment from Discord messages; two LSTM models (price-only vs. multi-modal with sentiment, volume, market cap) are compared for return forecasting.
result: Community sentiment is predominantly neutral with positive skew; the multi-modal LSTM significantly outperforms the price-only baseline in prediction accuracy.
conclusion: Community-derived signals have predictive value for virtual economy forecasting, suggesting future work at the intersection of virtual environments, NLP, and crypto market analysis.

title: Computing Gamma(p/q) With Beta Function Values
authors: Jan L\"ugering
abstract: ArXiv:2605.22888v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this expository article we show explicitly how to compute Gamma(p/q) in terms of Beta function values which in turn are Kontsevich-Zagier Periods.
tldr: This paper shows how to compute Gamma(p/q) using Beta function values, which are Kontsevich-Zagier periods.
motivation: The paper aims to provide an explicit method for computing Gamma(p/q) in terms of Beta function values, connecting to the theory of periods.
method: The author uses known identities relating Gamma and Beta functions and expresses the results in terms of Kontsevich-Zagier periods.
result: Gamma(p/q) can be expressed as a product of Beta function values, which are periods.
conclusion: The work is expository and does not present new results; it may be of interest to number theorists but not to the user's research areas.

title: An Optimal First-order Method For Smooth And Strongly Convex Composite Optimization And Its Stationary Limit
authors: Manu Upadhyaya, Daniel Berg Thomsen, Aymeric Dieuleveut, Adrien B. Taylor
abstract: ArXiv:2605.22929v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce Prox-ITEM, an optimal proximal gradient method for minimizing [MATH], where [MATH] is smooth and strongly convex, and [MATH] is convex, proper, and lower semicontinuous. In the smooth case [MATH], Prox-ITEM reduces to the information-theoretic exact method (ITEM). We prove an exact distance-to-solution bound for Prox-ITEM with the same distance-convergence rate as ITEM, and show that this rate is minimax optimal among span-based first-order methods using the same number of gradient-oracle calls for [MATH] and an arbitrary number of proximal-oracle calls for [MATH]. We also identify the stationary limit of Prox-ITEM, denoted Prox-TMM, which gives a proximal extension of the triple momentum method (TMM) to the composite setting and achieves the corresponding TMM distance-convergence rate.
