tldr: This paper proposes an optimal first-order method for smooth and strongly convex composite optimization, with no connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: To develop an optimal proximal gradient method for composite optimization problems that achieves minimax optimal convergence rates.
method: The authors introduce Prox-ITEM, a proximal extension of the information-theoretic exact method (ITEM), and analyze its convergence using distance-to-solution bounds.
result: Prox-ITEM achieves the same distance-convergence rate as ITEM and is minimax optimal among span-based first-order methods. Its stationary limit, Prox-TMM, extends the triple momentum method to composite settings.
conclusion: The work provides theoretically optimal algorithms for composite optimization, but has no direct application to the user's research interests.

title: Dichotomies Faster Or Slower Than Exponential Are Irrelevant For Skew-Product Flows
authors: N\'estor Jara, Iacopo P. Longo, Martin Rasmussen
abstract: ArXiv:2605.23173v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that dichotomies given by growth rates that are either faster or slower than exponential either do not occur or are inconsequential in the setting of skew-products with compact base. A similar conclusion is obtained for the nonuniform exponential behavior. To achieve this, we study families of translated linear nonautonomous differential equations for which we prove propagation results. We also study translations of growth rates under a comparison criteria.
tldr: The paper proves that dichotomies with growth rates faster or slower than exponential are irrelevant for skew-product flows with compact base.
motivation: To understand the role of exponential dichotomies in dynamical systems and to show that non-exponential growth rates do not lead to new phenomena.
method: The authors study families of translated linear nonautonomous differential equations and prove propagation results for dichotomies under comparison criteria.
result: Dichotomies with growth rates faster or slower than exponential either do not occur or are inconsequential in skew-product flows with compact base; similar for nonuniform exponential behavior.
conclusion: The findings simplify the theory of dichotomies by showing that only exponential dichotomies matter in this setting, with implications for the study of linear nonautonomous systems.

authors: Lo\"ic Constantin, Carlota M. Cuesta, Francisco de la Hoz

title: Mds And Nmds Codes From The Extended Twisted Generalized Reed-Solomon Codes
authors: Yanli Wang, Yanxin Chen, Tongjiang Yan
abstract: ArXiv:2605.23329v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper contributes to maximum distance separable (MDS) and near MDS (NMDS) properties of the extended generalized twisted Reed-Solomon (TGRS) codes. Firstly, a family of extended TGRS (ETGRS) are constructed by appending three columns to the generator matrix of original TGRS codes. Secondly, the necessary and sufficient conditions for these codes to be MDS or almost MDS (AMDS) codes are derived. Then, by analyzing the AMDS properties of their dual codes, the necessary and sufffcient conditions for them to be NMDS codes are established. Furthermore, some examples are given to verify the main results. Finally, we determine the non-generalized Reed-Solomon (non-GRS) characteristics of them via the Schur product method.
tldr: This paper constructs extended twisted generalized Reed-Solomon codes and derives conditions for them to be MDS or NMDS codes.
motivation: To expand the family of MDS and NMDS codes, which are important in coding theory for error correction.
method: The authors append three columns to the generator matrix of TGRS codes to obtain ETGRS codes, then derive necessary and sufficient conditions for MDS/AMDS/NMDS properties using algebraic methods and Schur product analysis.
result: Necessary and sufficient conditions for ETGRS codes to be MDS, AMDS, or NMDS are established, and examples verify the results. The codes are shown to be non-GRS via Schur product.
conclusion: The work provides new families of MDS and NMDS codes, contributing to coding theory, but has no direct connection to the user's research interests.

title: A High-order Nodally Bound-preserving And Mass-conservative Method For Linear Fourth-order Elliptic Problems And Its Applications To Nonlinear Parabolic Equations
authors: Zuodong Wang Jie Shen
abstract: ArXiv:2605.23486v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We propose a high-order finite element method for linear fourth-order elliptic problems that is both nodally bound-preserving and mass-conservative, based on a variational inequality formulation. The method admits an equivalent strictly convex minimization structure, which ensures well-posedness and enables an optimal error estimate in the [MATH]-seminorm, under suitable regularity assumptions. This framework is further extended to nonlinear fourth-order parabolic problems through space--time high-order discretizations that combine variational inequalities, BDF schemes, and scalar auxiliary variable (SAV) techniques. The fully discrete schemes preserve nodal bounds and mass, and a modified energy stability result is established for the first-order temporal scheme. We also apply the same framework to nonlinear second-order parabolic problems by introducing a consistent fourth-order regularization, leading to space--time high-order schemes with the same bound-preserving and mass-conservative properties. Extensive numerical results, including challenging tests with singularities and low regularity, demonstrate the stability, efficiency, and high-order accuracy of the proposed methods.
tldr: A high-order finite element method for fourth-order elliptic and parabolic problems that preserves nodal bounds and mass.
motivation: To develop numerical methods that maintain physical bounds and conservation laws for high-order PDEs.
method: Combines variational inequality formulation, BDF schemes, and scalar auxiliary variable (SAV) techniques.
result: The method achieves optimal error estimates, preserves nodal bounds and mass, and demonstrates stability and accuracy in numerical tests.
conclusion: The framework can be extended to nonlinear parabolic problems and second-order problems via regularization, with potential for broader applications.

title: Unlocking The Informational Value Of Marginal Costs For Exact Time Series Aggregation In Generation Expansion Planning
authors: Sonja Wogrin Luca Santosuosso
abstract: ArXiv:2605.23589v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper addresses the generation expansion planning (GEP) problem, formulated as a mixed-integer linear programming model with intertemporal storage constraints. Being generally NP-hard, the problem's computational complexity grows sharply with the planning horizon and the number of binary variables. While previous research has tackled this challenge using heuristic time series aggregation (TSA) methods, we propose a theoretically grounded marginal-cost-based TSA, designed to construct an aggregated model that preserves the active constraints of its full-scale counterpart, thereby explicitly targeting exact temporal aggregation. This TSA method is embedded within solution algorithms that iteratively refine theoretically validated bounds on the maximum error introduced by the temporal aggregation relative to conventional full-scale optimization, thus offering a formal performance guarantee to the decision-maker. Numerical results highlight the computational advantages of the proposed algorithms, which notably recover tractability whereas full-scale optimization proves intractable.
tldr: This paper proposes a marginal-cost-based time series aggregation method for generation expansion planning, a power systems optimization problem, with no connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: Generation expansion planning is computationally hard due to integer variables and long horizons; existing heuristic aggregation methods lack theoretical guarantees.
method: The authors develop a theoretically grounded marginal-cost-based time series aggregation that preserves active constraints of the full model, embedded in iterative algorithms with error bounds.
result: The proposed algorithms recover tractability where full-scale optimization is intractable, with formal performance guarantees.
conclusion: The method offers a principled approach to temporal aggregation in power systems planning, but its relevance to quantum computing or information thermodynamics is negligible.

title: A Unifying Approach To Closed Subspaces Of Linear And Multilinear Operators
authors: Ariel Mon\c{c}\~ao Geraldo Botelho
abstract: ArXiv:2605.23606v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove several abstract results giving general conditions under which subspaces of linear or multilinear operators on Banach spaces or Banach lattices are closed. Each of these abstract results is followed by concrete applications, concerning classes of linear/multilinear operators already studied as well as new classes.
tldr: This paper presents abstract conditions for closed subspaces of linear and multilinear operators on Banach spaces and lattices, with applications to operator classes.
motivation: To unify and generalize results on closedness of operator subspaces, which is a fundamental question in functional analysis.
method: Proves abstract theorems using Banach space theory and applies them to concrete classes of linear and multilinear operators.
result: Provides general conditions under which subspaces of operators are closed, with examples including new and existing operator classes.
conclusion: The work offers a unifying framework that may simplify proofs of closedness for various operator ideals, but its direct relevance to quantum information or thermodynamics is minimal.

title: Byot-cps: A Hybrid Cyber-Physical Systems Testbed For IoT Security Assessment And Platform Evaluation
authors: Nelson Che Neba Yan Lin Aung
abstract: ArXiv:2605.23059v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Internet of Things (IoT) security research continues to face a methodological gap between scalable virtual experimentation and realistic device behaviour. While pure simulation and emulation platforms provide control, repeatability, and scale, they do not fully reproduce firmware-specific behaviours, hardware characteristics, and vendor implementation weaknesses that frequently determine real-world exploitability. Conversely, physicalonly testbeds provide realism but are costly to assemble, difficult to reconfigure, and hard to replicate across institutions. This paper presents Build Your Own Cyber-Physical Systems Testbed (BYOT-CPS), a hybrid cyber-physical testbed that connects real IoT devices to virtualised network infrastructure built on GNS3. BYOT-CPS is designed to support security experimentation, education, and independent evaluation of commercial IoT security platforms within a controlled environment that preserves authentic device behaviour. Six requirements for such a testbed are defined: fidelity, heterogeneity, scalability, reproducibility, extensibility, and independence. A prototype deployment integrating smart bulbs, smart plugs, switches, and IP cameras with virtual enterprise, server, attack, and monitoring zones is used to demonstrate hybrid connectivity, penetration testing workflows, a Mirai-style denial-of-service attack, traffic monitoring, and controlled device manipulation. The evidence presented constitutes a feasibility validation of the framework rather than a largescale comparative benchmark. Within that scope, BYOT-CPS offers a practical middle ground between emulation-only research environments and costly physical laboratories while positioning vendor-neutral platform evaluation as a forward-looking design objective.
tldr: This paper presents a hybrid cyber-physical testbed for IoT security assessment, combining real devices with virtualized network infrastructure.
motivation: There is a gap between scalable virtual experimentation and realistic device behavior in IoT security research.
method: The authors built a hybrid testbed (BYOT-CPS) using GNS3 to connect real IoT devices with virtual enterprise, server, attack, and monitoring zones.
result: The prototype demonstrated hybrid connectivity, penetration testing, a Mirai-style DDoS attack, traffic monitoring, and device manipulation, validating the framework's feasibility.
conclusion: BYOT-CPS offers a practical middle ground between emulation-only environments and physical labs, with future work on vendor-neutral platform evaluation.

title: Prompt Overflow: What The Guardrail Inspects Is Not What The Model Infers
authors: Yuanbo Zhou, Changjia Zhu, Junyu Wang, Xu He, Yan Zhai, Kun Sun, Mingkui Wei, Junjie Xiong
abstract: ArXiv:2605.23196v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Guardrail models (a.k.a. safety checkers) are widely deployed to screen user inputs before they reach large language models (LLMs), serving as a primary defense against prompt injection attacks. Due to strict context constraints, these models handle overlength prompts through truncation or segmentation-based inspection. While prior work has focused on semantic adversarial inputs, the security implications of these long-input processing mechanisms remain largely unexplored. In this paper, we identify a critical blind spot arising from the mismatch between the limited inspection windows of guardrail models and the substantially larger context inference windows of downstream LLMs. We introduce a novel Prompt Overflow Attack, which exploits this mismatch by fragmenting malicious instructions and interleaving them with benign filler content across an overlong prompt, such that no individual inspected segment appears malicious while the full context remains actionable to the LLM. Through a systematic evaluation against state-of-the-art guardrail models, including Meta Llama Prompt Guard, IBM Granite Guardian, and DeBERTa-based detectors, we demonstrate that prompts reliably detected in short-context settings can evade guardrail models once adversarially manipulated into over-length inputs, yet remain fully actionable by downstream LLMs. We further propose potential defense strategies and outline mitigation directions to strengthen guardrail models.
tldr: This paper identifies a security vulnerability in guardrail models for LLMs where overlong prompts can bypass safety checks due to context window mismatches.
motivation: To expose a blind spot in guardrail models that inspect only truncated or segmented portions of long prompts, allowing malicious instructions to evade detection.
method: The authors propose a Prompt Overflow Attack that fragments malicious instructions and interleaves them with benign filler across an overlong prompt, then evaluate against state-of-the-art guardrail models.
result: Prompts that are reliably detected in short-context settings can evade guardrail models when adversarially manipulated into over-length inputs, yet remain actionable by downstream LLMs.
conclusion: The findings highlight the need for defense strategies such as dynamic context windows or multi-pass inspection to strengthen guardrail models against such attacks.

title: Arrow-Type Impossibility For Genuinely Modal Judgments
authors: Hirotaka Ono Yutaka Nagai
abstract: ArXiv:2605.23321v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Judgment aggregation studies how to combine individual judgments on logically related propositions into a collective judgment. Classical impossibility results show that sufficiently strong logical interconnections force dictatorship under natural aggregation axioms. In this paper, we ask whether such impossibility can still arise when the objects of aggregation are required to be genuinely modal judgments rather than plain factual propositions. Since modal logic contains propositional logic, this question is meaningful only if one excludes fact-based aggregation in disguise. We show that Arrow-type impossibility already re-emerges in a strikingly sparse modal setting. We prove an impossibility theorem on a simple cyclic frame for an agenda generated from a single propositional variable by repeated applications of a single modal operator, and we further demonstrate this phenomenon for an alternative family of frames satisfying a natural symmetry condition. Thus, even under a modal-operator requirement, semantic structure alone can generate the logical interconnections needed for dictatorship. Technically, our analysis has two layers. First, we prove a semantic reduction theorem showing that certain iterated modal patterns can be collapsed by shifting the evaluation point. Second, building on this reduction, we identify a local-to-global frame mechanism by which frame geometry yields minimally inconsistent modal judgment sets and the strong path-connectivity required for impossibility. The same reduction also turns consistency checking into a small combinatorial covering problem, which yields efficient implementations of non-dictatorial aggregation procedures.
tldr: This paper proves Arrow-type impossibility theorems for judgment aggregation when judgments are required to be genuinely modal, showing that even minimal modal structure can force dictatorship.
motivation: To determine whether classical impossibility results in judgment aggregation extend to settings where judgments are modal rather than purely factual, and to understand the minimal logical structure needed for such impossibility.
method: The authors use a semantic reduction theorem to collapse iterated modal patterns and a local-to-global frame mechanism to identify minimally inconsistent modal judgment sets and strong path-connectivity.
result: Arrow-type impossibility emerges even in a simple cyclic frame with a single propositional variable and a single modal operator, and also in other symmetric frames.
conclusion: Modal structure alone can generate the logical interconnections needed for dictatorship, and the reduction technique enables efficient non-dictatorial aggregation procedures.

title: Ai Security Research Should Better Incentivize Defense Research
authors: Youqian Zhang
abstract: ArXiv:2605.23448v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This work examines an imbalance in artificial intelligence (AI) security research: the field tends to produce more work on attacking AI systems than on defending them. Drawing on related academic papers, we find biased attack-to-defense ratios across subfields, including federated learning, speech recognition, membership inference, large language models, etc. The imbalance possibly means far beyond a simple count: attack papers are routinely evaluated under favorable conditions that make threats look more severe than they are in practice, while defenses are held to a stricter standard that few can meet. The result is a literature rich in demonstrated vulnerabilities and thin on usable and deployed protections. We thus argue that AI security research should better incentivize defense research.
tldr: This paper argues that AI security research is biased towards attack papers over defense papers, and calls for better incentives for defense research.
motivation: To highlight the imbalance in AI security research where attack papers outnumber defense papers, and to argue that this imbalance undermines practical security.
method: The paper reviews related academic papers and analyzes attack-to-defense ratios across subfields such as federated learning, speech recognition, membership inference, and large language models.
result: The analysis finds biased attack-to-defense ratios, with attack papers often evaluated under favorable conditions while defenses are held to stricter standards.
conclusion: The field should incentivize more defense research to produce usable and deployed protections.

title: CachePrune: Privacy-Aware And Fine-Grained Kv Cache Sharing For Efficient Llm Inference
authors: Guanlong Wu, Zhaohan Li, Yao Zhang, Zheng Zhang, Jianyu Niu, Ye Wu, Yinqian Zhang
abstract: ArXiv:2605.23640v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) rely on Key-Value (KV) caching to accelerate inference, and many serving systems further share the KV cache across users' requests to reduce redundant computation. While widely adopted, unrestricted cross-user sharing introduces side-channel vulnerabilities, allowing an adversary to infer user inputs by probing for cache reuse. Existing defenses disable sharing entirely to prevent leakage; yet such a coarse-grained strategy sacrifices substantial reuse potential, since prompts often include large portions of privacy-irrelevant segments, such as system instructions or publicly accessible materials. Building on this, we present CachePrune, a privacy-aware KV cache sharing mechanism that enables fine-grained reuse of KV entries across requests. Realizing such fine granularity requires token-level cache management, as reusable segments vary in length and position due to sensitivity masking, making reuse more complex than the fixed-size or sentence-level chunking used in existing coarse-grained schemes. Specifically, CachePrune makes fine-grained reuse practical by addressing two key challenges: accurately and efficiently deriving reusable KV segments and efficiently retrieving them over variable-length spans. We implement CachePrune on top of vLLM and evaluate it on three datasets, showing that it eliminates direct leakage through KV cache reuse side channels while reducing TTFT by 4.5x and increasing cache hit rates by 44% compared with state-of-the-art approaches.
tldr: CachePrune proposes a privacy-aware KV cache sharing mechanism for LLM inference that enables fine-grained reuse of non-sensitive tokens to improve efficiency while preventing side-channel attacks.
motivation: Existing KV cache sharing across users in LLM serving systems introduces side-channel vulnerabilities that leak user inputs, and current defenses disable sharing entirely, sacrificing performance.
method: CachePrune uses token-level cache management to identify and reuse only privacy-irrelevant segments (e.g., system instructions) by addressing challenges in deriving reusable segments and retrieving them over variable-length spans.
result: CachePrune eliminates direct leakage through KV cache reuse side channels while reducing time-to-first-token (TTFT) by 4.5x and increasing cache hit rates by 44% compared to state-of-the-art approaches.
conclusion: The work demonstrates that fine-grained privacy-aware KV cache sharing is feasible and beneficial, but its focus is on LLM inference security and efficiency, not on the user's research interests.

title: Validating Threat Modeling Results With The Help Of Vulnerable Test Applications
authors: Oleksandr Adamov, Davide Fucci, Felix Viktor Jedrzejewski, Ricardo Britto, Nishrith Saini
abstract: ArXiv:2605.23695v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Validating threat modeling results remains difficult because completeness is hard to judge without an external oracle. Existing studies often rely on expert-produced reference models and other human baselines, but these can contain omissions or disagreements. This paper evaluates a complementary, vulnerability-grounded validation approach. We apply threat modeling to intentionally vulnerable applications with a known vulnerability set to measure the number of related vulnerabilities that can be discovered. We compare ThreMoLIA, an LLM-assisted threat modeling solution developed by our team, with the Microsoft Threat Modeling Tool (MTMT) across two vulnerable applications: AzureGoat and the Vulnerable Bank Application (VulnBank). The inputs to both tools are limited to architecture, data flow diagrams, and their descriptions. The results show that ThreMoLIA achieved higher vulnerability coverage on both systems. We show that vulnerable test applications provide a practical benchmark for assessing threat coverage and complement expert-based validation.
tldr: This paper evaluates an LLM-assisted threat modeling tool using vulnerable test applications, showing improved vulnerability coverage over a traditional tool.
motivation: Validating threat modeling results is difficult due to lack of ground truth; existing expert-based validation may have omissions.
method: The authors compare their LLM-assisted tool ThreMoLIA with Microsoft Threat Modeling Tool on two intentionally vulnerable applications, measuring how many known vulnerabilities each tool discovers.
result: ThreMoLIA achieved higher vulnerability coverage on both AzureGoat and VulnBank compared to MTMT.
conclusion: Vulnerable test applications provide a practical benchmark for threat coverage and complement expert-based validation.

title: Reconstructibility Of Pitch Class Graphs And The Z-relation
authors: Aleksa Joksimovi\'c
abstract: ArXiv:2605.22948v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper gives a structural explanation for the Z-relation by modelling pitch-class sets as complete weighted graphs and encoding their interval content in a composition of [MATH] via an additivity rule. We introduce the realization number [MATH] -- the count of T/I-inequivalent compositions producing the same interval multiset [MATH] -- and show that Z-relation is precisely the condition [MATH]. We prove that Z-relation cannot occur at cardinality [MATH] in any [MATH], construct an explicit primitive Z-related pair at [MATH] for every [MATH] divisible by [MATH] with [MATH], and establish a Scaling Theorem showing that any Z-pair in [MATH] propagates to [MATH] for all [MATH]. All results are verified computationally for [MATH] and [MATH].
tldr: This paper studies the Z-relation in music theory using graph theory and combinatorial methods, with no connection to quantum information or physics.
motivation: To provide a structural explanation for the Z-relation among pitch-class sets, which is a concept in music theory.
method: Models pitch-class sets as complete weighted graphs and encodes interval content via an additivity rule; introduces realization number and uses combinatorial proofs and computational verification.
